history.summary: Ambika Niketan Temple was established in 1969 by the late Smt. Bharati Maiya, a devotee of Goddess Ambika. Dedicated to Ashtabhuja (eight-armed) Ambika, a form of the Mother Goddess, it stands on the banks of the Tapi River on Dumas Road at Parle Point, Athwalines. The simple two-storey structure has the main shrine on the first floor and an idol of Bharati Maiya on the ground floor, with smaller shrines to Shiva, Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Hanuman, and Lakshmi-Narayana. Travel sources describe it as one of Surat's most important Shakti pilgrimage centres (one calls it the second-most significant Shakti Puja centre after Aarasur Ambaji), drawing crowds year-round and especially during Navratri.

town_description: Surat is a major city in Gujarat on the banks of the Tapi River, historically one of India's most important ports under Mughal and then British rule. Today it is a thriving metropolis known worldwide as a diamond-processing and textile-manufacturing hub. The city grew from a 12th-century settlement into a Mughal port and later a British stronghold, retaining colonial-era landmarks, old-city bazaars, and a fast-developing riverfront. It is well connected by air, rail, and road to Mumbai, Vadodara, and the rest of Gujarat.
